Probably not—despite being geometrically above the horizon.

At **12:30 PM in bright daylight**, this **25%-illuminated waning crescent** would be only about **16° high**. Its **60° separation from the Sun** helps, but the low altitude substantially reduces contrast through atmospheric scattering and extinction. With normal unaided eyesight and only a rough idea where to look, spotting it would be **very difficult and unlikely**, though not physically impossible under exceptionally transparent conditions.

So if your concern is whether it would be conspicuous: **no—it almost certainly wouldn’t be noticeable unless you deliberately searched very carefully, ideally using binoculars to locate it first**. Never sweep with binoculars anywhere near the Sun; at a 60° separation it is well away, but keep the Sun completely out of the field.
